subject: general
question: Surendra buys mangoes at the rate of 3 kg for Rs. 21 and sells them at 5 kg for Rs. 50. To earn Rs. 102 as profit, he must sell:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equate the **quantity** of mangoes to find the profit per unit cycle.

CP of 3 kg = Rs. 21 ⇒ CP of 15 kg = 21 × 5 = Rs. 105.

SP of 5 kg = Rs. 50 ⇒ SP of 15 kg = 50 × 3 = Rs. 150.

Profit on 15 kg = 150 − 105 = Rs. 45.

Quantity for Rs. 102 profit = (15 ÷ 45) × 102 = 34 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 34 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** CP rate = 3 kg for Rs. 21 | SP rate = 5 kg for Rs. 50 | Target Profit = Rs. 102.

**Formulas:** CP per kg = Total Price ÷ Total Quantity | Profit per kg = SP per kg − CP per kg | Required Quantity = Total Profit ÷ Profit per kg.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/943989e07615131832acfe38db7bff0ea4443319ca51e92d42a665b94de4087f.png] 

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** per kg = 21 ÷ 3 = **Rs. 7 per kg**.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** per kg = 50 ÷ 5 = **Rs. 10 per kg**.

⇒ **Profit** per kg = SP − CP = 10 − 7 = **Rs. 3 per kg**.

⇒ Total quantity to be sold = Total Profit ÷ Profit per kg = 102 ÷ 3 = **34 kg**.

**∴ The correct answer is 34 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unitary Method in Profit and Loss

Calculating the price of a single unit helps in comparing buying and selling rates easily. Formula: Price per unit = Total Cost ÷ Total Units.

Profit Margin Calculation

Profit Percentage = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100. In this case: (3 ÷ 7) × 100 ≈ 42.85%.</p
